decision.summary: The current gas safety record (CP12 issued 2025-10-17, expires 2026-10-16) is still valid today, so the property is compliant. The legacy note "renewed 2025, all good" agrees but is superseded by the signed certificate. Ticket JOB-101 was opened and assigned to HeatRight Ltd, the tenant, landlord and contractor were contacted, and the job is on hold until 2026-10-12 for the tenant's access reply.

answers.question: Is the property currently compliant for gas safety? Which record do you trust and why?
answers.answer: Yes, as of today (2026-10-10). I trust the current signed CP12 record (CP12_2025.pdf, issued 2025-10-17, expires 2026-10-16, Gas Safe 550123). The legacy note saying 'renewed 2025, all good' is an old-agency comment with no expiry date, so it is secondary. The certificate lapses on 2026-10-16 unless renewed.

answers.question: What steps do you take to get access lawfully before expiry?
answers.answer: Opened JOB-101 and assigned HeatRight Ltd. Emailed the tenant asking for an access time, with 24h written notice and no entry without agreement. Asked HeatRight to book before 16 Oct. Held the job until 2026-10-12 to review. If there is still no reply, phone the tenant and escalate to maintenance at P2. Do not enter without 24h written notice or an emergency.

answers.question: What do you tell the landlord?
answers.answer: That the CP12 is valid until 16 Oct 2026, the tenant has not replied, HeatRight has been asked to book before expiry, and we will call before booking anything above £300 inc VAT, his spend limit.

assumptions: The CP12 cost is expected to be within the £300 limit but this is unconfirmed.
The emails and SMS went to the contact details on file for the tenant.
The HeatRight request was sent through the phone-call channel as a message; no phone call was logged as made.

If you have any questions, please reply here.

Kind regards,
Lettings Operations
